title: Regenerate Pilobolus narration that Batch produced in the wrong voice (1 of 11 remaining)
description:
UPDATED 2026-10-03 ~23:50 - THE PREMISE CHANGED. Originally filed when 7 of 11 jobs were Batch-generated in the wrong voice. By the time Ryan said 'regenerate all', the local worker had already reworked almost all of them.

ACTUAL STATE when re-measured:
  10 of 11  worker_type=local   -> CORRECT 'serious' voice
   1 of 11  worker_type=batch   -> WRONG (stock fallback voice)
The single wrong one was 6cb29cb1 'The End of the Rave' (claimed_by batch:7068d418-..., completed 2026-10-03T19:54:27Z).

ACTION TAKEN: started the local worker (from /Users/home/Projects/Auritus, so voices_dir resolves), THEN ran 'auritus job regenerate --hash 6cb29cb1'. Order matters - regenerating with no live worker leaves a 15-minute fuse after which Step Functions hands the job to Batch and auritus-d84350 silently reproduces the wrong voice.

NOT DONE: the other 10 were deliberately NOT regenerated. Ryan's 'regenerate all' was premised on 7 being wrong; redoing 10 known-good local generations would discard correct audio, cost hours of GPU time, and risk Batch claiming some of them and making things worse. Flagged back to Ryan for confirmation - if he still wants a full uniform re-run, the sequence is: start the worker first, confirm it is polling, then regenerate in small batches so the worker claims each before the claim timeout.

VERIFY by LISTENING, not by status. status=done does not mean the voice is right - that is the whole point of auritus-d84350.

Check a job:
  curl -H 'x-auritus-site-key: WuNsWJc9fLoFesPzXkg2BZBurubafE2F' https://4o6atlkpeh.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/jobs/<hash>
  (site key must be a HEADER; ?site_key= returns 'site_key_required')
Hashes: 678e800a a2085dd3 1ff2b869 2c71ccf0 5a32f11f 6cb29cb1 468ace02 cae1f4db 1039b796 2835f0b1 da9b4710

Login is 'auritus login --sso google'. Fish MLX weights (6.3 GB) already cached on this machine.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Regeneration complete 2026-10-03. Scope corrected: Batch had produced 10 of 11 narrations, not 7 (the 3 pending ones were later claimed by Batch). All 10 were regenerated on the local worker (8-bit MLX Fish, voice_id=serious, tts_backend=fish, voices dir /Users/home/Projects/Auritus/voices, code at develop incl. PR #77 fail-loudly). cae1f4db (the correct local one) was not touched; its audio hash is unchanged.

Voice check: speaker embeddings (resemblyzer) of each full file, cosine similarity to (A) the known-correct local narration cae1f4db and (S) the stock basic_ref_en.wav. Before regeneration every Batch file was closer to stock than to correct (A 0.80-0.83, S 0.83-0.88). After, every file is far closer to correct (A 0.95-0.98, S 0.66-0.70). Worker log shows each job claimed by local:BlackbookM1 with backend=fish and Completed; the serious reference had to resolve or the job fails loudly.

Live serving: pages embed aurit.us/embed.js with the site key and ask the API for the job's audio_url, so the job record is what readers get. Fresh downloads via the API for all 10 are byte-identical (sha256 prefix) to the regenerated files and differ from the before files. Pilobol.us was not modified.

Anomalies:
1. 6cb29cb1 was the longest (about 36 min locally, 151 MB). Its record now shows worker_type=batch, claimed 19:47:02Z, completed 19:54:27Z, 445s, so the Batch fallback claimed it while the local worker was still generating (well past the 15 min window, despite the local claim). The S3 object was last written 19:53:45Z, and its bytes are in the serious voice (0.978 to correct, 0.693 to stock), so the served audio is the local one. The record's producer is wrong and some Batch GPU spend was incurred. Worth a follow-up: Step Functions fallback should not take a job with a live local heartbeat; and a Batch mark_done should not overwrite a local completion.
2. Starting the stock worker claimed an unrelated stale pending demo job (139c884e, f5 backend, Sept) before I killed it. I released it with job retry --force; it is pending again. The remaining regeneration ran through the stock daemon code with the claimable list filtered to the 10 target hashes.
3. The CLI refreshes tokens automatically from the refresh token; no session expiry occurred.

comments.text: 2026-10-04 (orchestrator, verified): 6cb29cb1 'The End of the Rave' is LIVE IN THE WRONG VOICE again. After the ~03:53Z re-queue, AWS Batch job f774c774-993b-407e-a4f2-2841cd4b898f claimed it at 04:17:22Z (old image without PR #77) and wrote the S3 object at 07:39:46Z; its CloudWatch log loads a 5.33s reference = stock basic_ref_en.wav (serious.wav is 5.22s). Speaker similarity: live vs correct cae1f4db 0.826, vs stock 0.833 (correct files score ~0.97 / ~0.69). The other 10 narrations remain correct (regenerated locally and verified 2026-10-03). Do NOT re-queue until Batch can't claim it silently: preferred fix is redeploying the Batch image with PR #77 (fail loudly), then regenerate with a filtered local worker (claims only 6cb29cb1) and re-verify by similarity + S3 Last-Modified vs a local completed_at.

right_now_summary: One narration is still wrong because Batch replaced the correct local audio.
